proposed_comments.title: Keep Game Mode detection out of the low-level mouse hook

confidence.rationale: The current upstream diff calls SHQueryUserNotificationState through detect_game_mode from MouseHookProc when the new option is enabled. Low-level hook callbacks are system input-path callbacks and should return quickly; this shell query is not a cached atomic read and can block input delivery.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep Game Mode detection out of the low-level mouse hook

**Severity:** `high`

When the new setting is enabled, `MouseHookProc` calls `detect_game_mode()`, which invokes `SHQueryUserNotificationState`, from the `WH_MOUSE_LL` callback. That callback runs on the system input path and needs to return quickly; doing a shell notification-state query there can stall mouse delivery or cause Windows to skip/remove the hook, especially when the user is actively moving across monitor edges. Please move the Game Mode query to module state updated outside the low-level hook (for example, a timer or worker that owns failure handling) and make the hook read only cached atomic state before deciding whether to wrap.
